UNDERSTAND YOUR MIND

What does an IQ test
actually measure?

IQ, or intelligence quotient, is one way to describe cognitive ability. Reasoning tasks explore how you spot patterns, process information, and solve unfamiliar problems.

Our 20 practice questions cover five areas: pattern recognition, visual counting, numerical reasoning, spatial reasoning, and abstract reasoning.

This is a recreational reasoning exercise, not a standardized assessment. Your practice score is not a clinical IQ score, and no single number defines your abilities.

Understanding IQ scores Illustration

A common scale: mean 100, standard deviation 15

A SCORE IS JUST ONE PERSPECTIVE

Making sense of IQ scores

Many standardized IQ scales use an average of 100 and a standard deviation of 15. In the corresponding normal distribution, about 68% of scores fall between 85 and 115.

Here, your results show how many questions you answered correctly and how you did in each skill area. We do not convert unvalidated results into IQ scores or population rankings.

Creativity, curiosity, emotional understanding, and a willingness to learn matter, too.

GOOD QUESTIONS DESERVE ANSWERS

FAQs

A few things to know before you begin.

Are the test and results really free?

Yes. All 20 questions, your practice score, your five-skill breakdown, and every explanation are free. There are no subscriptions or paid results.

Will this tell me my actual IQ?

No. This is a recreational exercise, not a professionally standardized assessment. Your score reflects your performance on these questions, not a clinical IQ measurement or diagnosis.

How long does the test take?

There are 20 questions and a 20-minute time limit. You can finish early. When time runs out, your answers are submitted automatically; unanswered questions earn no points.

What kinds of questions are included?

The test covers pattern recognition, visual counting, numerical reasoning, spatial reasoning, and abstract reasoning. Each question has four answer choices.

Do I need an account or email address?

No. You can start right away. Your answers are saved only in your current browser and are not uploaded to a server. The test does not ask for your name or email.

Can I refresh the page and continue?

Yes, if your browser allows local storage. Your progress is saved automatically, and the timer keeps running. If the 20 minutes expire while the page is closed, your results will be calculated when you return.

Can I skip questions or change my answers?

Yes. Selecting an answer automatically takes you to the next question. Use Previous or a question number to return and make changes. You can also skip a question. After question 20, review your answers before submitting.

Can I take the test again?

Yes. Select Try again on your results page. You will see the same questions, so familiarity may improve your score. That does not mean your IQ has changed.
